2027-04-12.title: Monday of the Third Week of Easter
readings: They could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which Stephen spoke; his face was like the face of an angel
Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord! (or: Alleluia)
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life
2027-04-12.alt: Easter weekday. The Alleluia sounds again at the Gospel acclamation; the Paschal candle is lit at the liturgy until Pentecost; the Regina Caeli takes the place of the Angelus. All this week the Gospel is the Bread of Life discourse of John 6. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-12.verse: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you.
theo: Stephen first appears in the Acts of the Apostles as a man chosen to wait on tables. The Twelve had asked the community to pick seven men “of good standing, full of the Spirit and of wisdom” to care for the daily distribution of food to the widows, so that the apostles could give themselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word. Stephen's name stands first on the list. But today we see that the man appointed to serve bread is also a man of the word: “full of grace and power,” he “did great wonders and signs among the people.” Members of the synagogue of the Freedmen, Jews from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia and Asia, begin to argue with him, and “they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.” When argument fails, accusation begins. False witnesses are brought: “This man never stops saying things against this holy place and the law.” St Luke tells the story so that we hear the trial of Jesus again; there too false witnesses spoke about the Temple (Mark 14:57–58). The disciple is walking the road of his Master. And at the very moment of accusation Luke gives us one quiet, luminous line: all who sat in the council looked at him, “and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.” The man accused of speaking against Moses carries the radiance of Moses, whose face shone when he came down from Sinai after speaking with God. The Psalm gives us Stephen's inner prayer: “Even though princes sit plotting against me, your servant will meditate on your statutes.” The quarrel here is a family quarrel among Jews, for Stephen is himself a Jew; Luke does not blame a whole people, and neither does the Church (Catechism 597).

The Gospel takes us to the morning after the feeding of the five thousand. The crowd has noticed that Jesus did not get into the boat with his disciples, so they take boats from Tiberias and cross to Capernaum looking for him. “Rabbi, when did you come here?” Jesus does not answer the question; he answers the heart: “you are looking for me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate your fill of the loaves.” They had seen bread; they had not seen the sign. They wanted another meal, not the One who gives it. So Jesus lifts their eyes: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you.” They reply like good, practical people: “What must we do to perform the works of God?” They expect a list. Jesus gives them one word: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.” Faith is both God's work in us and our first work for God; every good deed grows out of it. Through this whole week the Church reads the great discourse on the Bread of Life, step by step, and in the Easter season we read it with the eyes of the newly baptized, who have just received the Eucharist for the first time. Stephen served the bread that perishes to hungry widows and preached the bread that endures. The Church still does both, and both are the work of love.
outline: Ask: why do I look for Jesus? For what he gives, or for himself?
Point 1 · A face like an angel
Stephen, calm and radiant under false accusation.
The crowd wanted loaves, not the Giver.
Point 3 · The one work God asks
Believe in him whom he has sent.
“Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.”
live: Work for the food that endures (John 6:27)
Give ten unhurried minutes today to the food that lasts: read John 6:22–40 slowly, or make a short visit to the Blessed Sacrament.
If someone speaks unfairly about you today, do not answer in kind. Stay calm like Stephen, and pray for that person by name.
2027-04-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, you filled your servant Stephen with grace and power and made his face shine before his accusers. Deliver us from seeking you only for the bread that perishes. Give us the faith that is your own work in us, and feed us with the bread that endures for eternal life, until we see your face in glory. Amen. Alleluia.
altar: The crowd wanted more loaves; Jesus wanted to give himself. At the altar he gives the food that endures for eternal life: his own Body and Blood, truly present under the appearances of bread and wine, set apart by the Father's seal.

quick: Stephen, full of grace and the Spirit, was falsely accused, and his face shone like an angel's.
The crowd looked for Jesus because they had eaten bread, not because they had understood the sign.
Jesus said: work for the food that endures; the work of God is to believe in the One he has sent.
2027-04-12.action: Spend ten quiet minutes today with John 6 or before the tabernacle.
2027-04-12.question: Do I come to Jesus mostly for what I want from him, or for him?

family.explain: After Jesus fed thousands of people with five loaves, the people went looking for him the next day. Jesus said: you are looking for me because you got bread to eat! But there is a better bread, one that lasts for ever, and I will give it to you. They asked: what must we do? Jesus said: believe in me.
family.intention: We pray for people who are hungry today, and for all who are hungry for God without knowing it.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing I usually ask Jesus for? Can I also tell him today that I love him, without asking anything?”

illus: A woman in Alappuzha ran a small tea shop beside a bus stand. For years she served morning tea to the same drivers and conductors, and she always kept a small picture of the Sacred Heart above the stove. One driver, a rough young man, asked her mockingly why she wasted money on candles in front of a picture. She said: you come here for tea because it keeps you awake till noon. I go to him because he keeps me alive for ever. The young man laughed. Two years later, after an accident that nearly killed him, he came to the shop, sat down without ordering anything, and asked her which church she went to.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Bread of Life, we have come looking for you. Purify our hearts so that we seek you for your own sake. Alleluia. Amen.
share: They saw that his face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). What gives a person that kind of peace under attack?
You are looking for me… because you ate your fill of the loaves (John 6:26). What do I mostly ask of Jesus?
This is the work of God, that you believe (John 6:29). How can my faith become my first work each day?
pm.resp: Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord! Alleluia.
interc: For Christians who are falsely accused or persecuted for their faith, that they may have Stephen's peace.
For deacons and all who serve the poor at the Church's tables.
For those who work hard only for the food that perishes, that they may find the bread that endures.
For the newly baptized of this Easter, that their faith may deepen week by week.
For our group, that we may seek Jesus for himself.
pm.close: Father, you set your seal on your Son and give him to us as the bread that endures. Make our faith strong and our faces bright with his peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Stephen was chosen to serve food to widows. A humble job. But the Spirit does not stay inside job descriptions: the man who served tables was full of grace and power, and his wisdom was so strong that his opponents could not answer him (Acts 6:10).

So they found false witnesses, as they had for Jesus. And at that moment, when anyone else would be angry or afraid, the whole council looked at Stephen and saw that his face was like the face of an angel (Acts 6:15). That is what Easter does to a person. The risen Lord gives a peace that accusations cannot take away.

In the Gospel a crowd crosses the lake looking for Jesus. It sounds wonderful, until Jesus tells them the truth: you are looking for me because you ate your fill of the loaves (John 6:26). They wanted more bread, not the One who gives it. Many of us pray like that: we come when we need something, and disappear when we have it.

Jesus does not send them away. He offers them more than they asked: work for the food that endures for eternal life. And when they ask what work they must do, he gives them one: believe in him whom God has sent (John 6:29). Faith first, and everything else grows from it. At this Mass he gives us that food that endures, his own Body and Blood. Let us seek him today not only for his gifts but for himself. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the people followed Jesus because he gave them bread to eat. Jesus said: I have an even better bread for you, a bread that makes you live for ever! That bread is Jesus himself, in Holy Communion. Today let us tell Jesus: I love you, not only for what you give me, but because you are you!

intro: Theme: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.”
Stephen's shining face, the crowd that wanted only bread, and the one work God asks of us.

sub: The table servant full of the Spirit.
False witnesses, as at the trial of Jesus.
The radiance of one who has been with God.
q: Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And all who sat in the council looked intently at him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
points.apply: Before a difficult conversation this week, spend a few minutes with the Lord first, and go in with his peace.

sub: Crossing the lake for more loaves.
The Giver greater than the gift.
q: Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and delight yourselves in rich food.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For it is on him that God the Father has set his seal.
points.apply: Look honestly at how you spend your best hours this week, and give one of them to the food that endures.

sub: Not a list but a person.
Faith as God's work in us.
q: I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I set your ordinances before me.
Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
points.apply: Begin each morning this week with a simple act of faith: Lord Jesus, I believe in you, whom the Father has sent.

concl: The Spirit made a table servant shine with the peace of the risen Lord.
Jesus calls us beyond the bread that perishes to faith in him, the bread that endures.
2027-04-12.resolve: Make an act of faith every morning this week and one visit to the Blessed Sacrament.
